input: Learn to identify edible mushrooms safely with a guide

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Are they trying to learn a handful of beginner-friendly species or build a broad identification repertoire? This determines how deep and wide the learning plan needs to be.
The region and ecosystem they forage in determines which species are relevant — mushrooms vary enormously by geography, climate, and habitat.
Whether they are learning solo, with a mentor, or as part of a group (e.g. mycological society) changes the resources and social structure of the plan.
Their available time — whether they want a quick crash course or a multi-season learning journey — shapes how intensive and sequential the plan should be.
Their preferred learning style (hands-on field work, books, apps, video courses) determines which guide formats and resources to recommend.
Knowing their end goal — confident solo foraging, cooking a specific mushroom, or passing a course — defines what 'done well' looks like and sets a clear target.
Whether they already own a field guide, have access to foraging groups, or are starting from scratch determines the very first concrete action to take.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to safely identify edible wild mushrooms
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to develop the ability to identify edible mushrooms safely, using some form of guide or structured resource.

questions.title: Which species do you most want to learn first?
questions.description: Are you aiming to identify just 2-3 iconic beginner species (e.g. chanterelles, porcini), or do you want to build a broad knowledge of many edible types over time?

questions.title: What region or habitat will you be foraging in?
questions.description: Identifying the geographic area and typical terrain (forest type, climate zone, country/state) ensures the species, guides, and toxic look-alikes covered are relevant to where you actually forage.

questions.title: Will you be learning solo or with an experienced forager?
questions.description: Knowing whether you have access to a mentor, a local mycological society, or guided foraging walks changes how the learning plan is structured and how quickly you can progress safely.

questions.title: How much time can you dedicate to this over what period?
questions.description: A few hours on weekends over one season requires a very different plan than a committed multi-year study — this sets the pace and depth of the learning journey.

questions.title: Do you prefer books, apps, videos, or field courses?
questions.description: Your preferred format for absorbing new knowledge determines which types of guides and resources to prioritise — printed field guides, identification apps, YouTube channels, or in-person workshops.

questions.title: What does confidently knowing a mushroom look like to you?
questions.description: Is the goal to forage and cook what you find independently, to pass a formal foraging certification, or simply to not misidentify something dangerous on a hike? This defines the finish line.

questions.title: Do you already own any field guides or foraging tools?
questions.description: Knowing your current starting resources — field guides, spore print kits, a hand lens, foraging basket — determines the very first practical step: what to acquire versus what to use right away.
